payload.analysis: Left upper eyelid biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy, strongly supporting cutaneous lupus erythematosus, especially with lupus nephritis and prior hydroxychloroquine toxicity. This favors lupus over eczema/seborrheic dermatitis or infection. DIF, serology, and culture remain missing, but all retrieved evidence is covered; cutaneous lupus flare is the leading diagnosis.

payload.report: A woman in her 70s with lupus nephritis and prior hydroxychloroquine toxicity presented with a one-month periorbital eruption of scaly, crusted pink plaques. Left eyelid biopsy showed vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy—typical of cutaneous lupus—refuting eczema and infection. With her systemic lupus history this confirms cutaneous lupus erythematosus; since immunofluorescence and cultures are unavailable, this is the finest achievable level.
